Baron Friedrich von Steuben. A Prussian officer who arrived at Valley Forge in 1778 and transformed the Continental Army from an undisciplined militia into a professional fighting force.

Steuben came as a volunteer, sponsored by Benjamin Franklin, claiming Prussian military credentials. He brought the rigid discipline and training methods of Frederick the Great's army to the American cause.

He created the first standardized drill manual for the Continental Army, teaching soldiers uniform tactics, discipline, and coordinated maneuvers that closed the professional gap with British redcoats. He also implemented rigorous inspection standards and sanitation protocols that reduced disease among the troops, directly saving hundreds of lives during the terrible winter of 1777 and 1778.

Despite his harsh discipline, enlisted men earned deep respect for him, winning their loyalty through fairness and his willingness to train alongside them in the freezing conditions. He remained with the Continental Army through the end of the war, coordinating infantry tactics at crucial engagements and modernizing American military organization.

After independence, he settled in America, where he was granted land in recognition of his service. He died a respected figure in the new nation he helped create through his genius for organization and training.
